Still reproduces on **1.18.11**, so the 0.4.x guardrail this issue was left open for has fired. `@opencode-ai/plugin@1.18.11` declares `@opentui/{core,solid,keymap}` peers as `>=0.4.5` and pins `0.4.5` in devDependencies.

My case isolates obstacle **(b)** (renderer-instance skew) cleanly from obstacle **(a)** (skipped Solid JSX transform), which I haven't seen reported separately, so adding the data point.

### Why (a) doesn't apply here

The plugin is **pre-bundled with tsup**, so the JSX is already compiled to `_$createElement(...)` calls in `dist/tui.js` and `@opentui/solid` is left `external`. There is no `@jsxImportSource` pragma and no `jsx-runtime` import at runtime, so the `node_modules` exclusion in `solid-plugin.js` is irrelevant, and I never hit the `Export named 'jsxDEV' not found` error. (b) alone is still fatal.

### Environment

- opencode **1.18.11**, Bun 1.3.13, Linux
- Installed via **`git+ssh://` spec** against a self-hosted GitLab (not the npm registry), so this isn't registry-specific:
  `"plugin": ["myplugin@git+ssh://git@gitlab.example.com:8086/group/sub/myplugin.git"]`
- Resolved inside `~/.cache/opencode/packages/<spec>/node_modules/`:
  `@opentui/solid 0.4.5`, `@opentui/core 0.4.5`, `solid-js 1.9.12`, i.e. **exactly the versions the host asks for**. This is instance/export-condition skew, not version skew.

### Symptoms

The plugin loads and runs fine: `tui(api)` executes, `api.slots.register({ slots: { sidebar_content } })` succeeds, and the host **does invoke the slot function**. Only rendering is broken.

1. Returning JSX with host elements throws:

```
Error: No renderer found
    at createElement (~/.cache/opencode/packages/<spec>/node_modules/@opentui/solid/src/reconciler.ts:196:17)
    at sidebar_content (~/.cache/opencode/packages/<spec>/node_modules/<pkg>/dist/tui.js:354:22)
```

2. Wrapping the slot's return value in `<RendererContext.Provider value={api.renderer}>`, using `RendererContext` imported from the **plugin's own** `@opentui/solid`, **silences the throw** (`api.renderer` is present), but nothing renders.

3. With the throw suppressed, **Solid reactivity is dead across the boundary**. A `createSignal` created in `tui(api)` and read inside `<Show when={accessor()}>` has its accessor evaluated **exactly once**, and never again after `setStatus(...)` fires from an async callback. Timestamps from the plugin's own log:

```
18:06:39.052  sidebar_content render called {"hasRenderer":true}
18:06:39.052  quotaOf read {"kind":"loading"}     <- first and only evaluation
18:06:39.466  quota ok {"used":3550,...}          <- setStatus() ran here; accessor never re-runs
```

That is consistent with the plugin's `solid-js` / `@opentui/solid` owner+context globals being a different module instance from the host's: the host renders in its universe, the plugin's memo subscribes in its own, and the two never meet.

### Control

The **identical `dist/tui.js`**, with the **same dependency versions present in its own `node_modules`**, renders and updates correctly when referenced by absolute path in `tui.json`:

```json
{ "plugin": ["/home/me/.config/opencode/plugins/myplugin/dist/tui.js"] }
```

So duplicate copies existing on disk isn't sufficient to break it. What matters is whether the plugin is loaded from **under `node_modules`**. Same files, same versions, different load path, opposite outcome.

### Note for other plugin authors landing here

Unrelated to this bug, but it cost me a while: if your `package.json` declares a `build` script, installing from a git spec makes pacote treat the plugin as needing a "prepare" step (`pacote/lib/git.js` `#prepareDir` triggers on `postinstall`/`build`/`preinstall`/`install`/`prepack`/`prepare`). It then clones and spawns a full `npm install`, which fails under the bundled binary with the opaque `git dep preparation failed`. Renaming the script to something off that list avoids it when you ship a committed `dist/`.

Confirmé este mismo root cause con un disparador distinto — sin VS Code de por medio, solo terminal + `opencode run`.

**Escenario:** un proceso `opencode` quedó suspendido con `Ctrl+Z` (estado `T`/`Tl` en `ps`, con hijos MCP también suspendidos) durante varios días sin cerrarse. Mientras ese proceso zombi seguía vivo, cualquier sesión nueva de `opencode` (TUI o `opencode run "<prompt>"`) tenía ~1 de cada 5 intentos que se colgaba indefinidamente sin ningún error visible — el log se detenía justo después de `"event connected"` y nunca llegaba a crear el step de la sesión.

Verificación:
```
$ ps aux | grep opencode
diegot3+  20118  0.7  1.1 ... Tl   jul31  24:32 opencode   # suspendido desde hace días
diegot3+ 190680  2.9  2.3 ... Sl+  11:49   2:02 opencode   # sesión activa

$ fuser ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db-wal
/home/.../opencode.db-wal:  20118 190680
```

Ambos PIDs (el zombi suspendido y el proceso activo) tenían el `-wal` abierto simultáneamente. Al matar el proceso zombi (`kill 20118`), el lock se liberó (`fuser` deja de reportar nada) y 8/8 pruebas posteriores con los mismos prompts que antes fallaban respondieron correctamente y de forma consistente (~7-11s cada una).

Descarté que fuera un problema de contenido/longitud del prompt: probé variando número de palabras, presencia de `?`, con/sin comillas — el fallo era puramente intermitente y correlacionaba 100% con la presencia del proceso zombi reteniendo el WAL, no con el prompt en sí.

Esto sugiere que el fix de `busy_timeout` propuesto aquí (o el fork `sst/opencode` con `busy_timeout=5000`) resolvería también este caso — cualquier escenario con 2+ procesos `opencode` abiertos sobre el mismo `opencode.db` (multi-ventana VS Code, terminal + proceso suspendido, `opencode run` en paralelo, etc.) parece compartir la misma causa raíz.

**Entorno:**
- OpenCode version: 1.18.10
- OS: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8.0-136-generic)
- Instalación: Homebrew

Independent reproduction, with a reconciliation against the provider's actual billing and a control group that isolates the cause to the missing `cache.write` count.

**Setup:** opencode 1.18.5, macOS, `opencode-go` provider (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`), headless `opencode run --format json`, no plugins, isolated `XDG_*` dirs. 63 automated sessions on 2026-07-31 across three models (21 each).

**Result for `gpt-5.6-luna`:** summing opencode's self-reported per-step `cost` gives **$0.1459**. The provider's own per-model daily billing view shows **$0.41** for the same model on the same day — a **2.8× understatement**.

Token totals opencode recorded across those 21 luna sessions:

```
input 414,350 · output 79,877 · reasoning 30,620 · cache.read 3,813,750 · cache.write 0
```

The gap is $0.2641. At luna's $0.125/M cache-write rate that implies **~2.11M unreported cache-write tokens**, against 3.81M recorded reads — a ~1.8:1 read:write ratio, which is what you'd expect from sessions with growing context. (As #36749 puts it: something had to write the prefix that is being read.)

**Control group — same gateway, same day, same harness:**

| model | cache-write rate | opencode self-reported | provider billing UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-5.6-luna` | $0.125/M | $0.1459 | **$0.41** ✗ |
| `deepseek-v4-flash` | none | $0.1138 | $0.12 ✓ |
| `mimo-v2.5` | none | $0.0882 | $0.11 ✓ |

This is the part I think is useful for triage: the two models that **don't** bill for cache writes reconcile with billing to the cent, and only the model that **does** is wrong. So this isn't general cost drift or a gateway-wide pricing mismatch — the error tracks exactly with whether cache writes are billable, which points at the missing `cache.write` count rather than at any rate.

Blast radius on this gateway is wider than luna: `qwen3.5-plus`, `qwen3.6-plus`, `qwen3.7-plus` and `qwen3.7-max` all carry cache-write rates as well, with `qwen3.7-max` at $3.125/M — above its own $2.50/M input rate.

Related: #39891 reports the same luna discrepancy via the TUI-vs-web comparison, and #36749 has the root cause on this code path (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` hardcodes `cacheWrite: void 0`, and `usage()` only reads `inputTokenDetails.cacheWriteTokens`) along with an offered fix.

@AliAltivate Thanks for digging into this. To answer your question: `vesper-ios` was **not** copied or cloned from `vesper`. They're independent repos with different GitHub remotes and different initial commits, and they resolve to different project IDs. Both have usable remotes, so `Project.resolve` returns the `git-remote:` hash and never reaches the root-commit fallback — that path isn't involved here.

You're also right that it isn't a name-prefix collision. But there is a real bug: my `project` table had two projects claiming the same worktree, with the real `vesper-ios` directory demoted to a sandbox of the iOS project. The trigger is a **renamed** repo, not a copied one.

## Cause

`fromDirectory` pins `worktree` permanently for every non-global project:

```ts
// packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts:237
worktree: projectID === ProjectV2.ID.global ? worktree : existing.worktree,
```

So when a repo is renamed or moved and reopened, the new path falls through to the sandbox branch instead of correcting the worktree:

```ts
// packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts:243-246
data.directory !== result.worktree &&
!result.sandboxes.includes(data.directory)
  ? result.sandboxes.push(data.directory)
```

`sandboxes` entries are pruned against the filesystem a few lines later, but `worktree` is never revalidated — so a stale path survives indefinitely, even once it belongs to a different repository.

The desktop symptom follows from there. `rootFor` (`packages/app/src/context/layout.tsx:473`) builds a sandbox → worktree map, so opening the renamed directory resolves back to the old path. And the effect at `layout.tsx:495-505` removes any open project whose `rootFor` differs from its own worktree, which is why the project wouldn't stay open at all. That accounts for both behaviors in my original report.

## Reproduction — no copying or cloning required

```
git init foo && cd foo && git remote add origin <some-url> && git commit --allow-empty -m init
# open foo in OpenCode Desktop
cd .. && mv foo bar
# open bar in OpenCode Desktop
```

`bar` is folded into `foo` as a sandbox, and the picker resolves it back to `foo`. Any rename or move of a tracked repo reproduces it; the names don't need to share a prefix.

I confirmed this against `fromDirectory` directly on `1882c33`. After the rename the project ID is stable, `worktree` stays on the old path — which no longer exists on disk — and the renamed directory is appended to `sandboxes`:

```
[repro] project id stable:   true
[repro] worktree after mv:   /…/T/opencode-test-xzwcavrmesm
[repro] renamed dir:         /…/T/opencode-test-xzwcavrmesm-renamed
[repro] sandboxes after mv:  ["/…/T/opencode-test-xzwcavrmesm-renamed"]
```

<details>
<summary>Test used (passes today, documenting current behavior)</summary>

```ts
it.live("renaming a tracked repo folds the new path into the old worktree", () =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const project = yield* Project.Service
    const tmp = yield* tmpdirScoped({ git: true })
    yield* Effect.promise(() => $`git remote add origin https://github.com/example/foo.git`.cwd(tmp).quiet())

    const first = yield* project.fromDirectory(tmp)
    expect(first.project.worktree).toBe(tmp)
    expect(first.project.sandboxes).toEqual([])

    const renamed = path.join(path.dirname(tmp), path.basename(tmp) + "-renamed")
    yield* Effect.promise(() => $`mv ${tmp} ${renamed}`.quiet())

    const second = yield* project.fromDirectory(renamed)

    expect(second.project.id).toBe(first.project.id)
    expect(second.project.worktree).toBe(tmp) // stale: this path is gone
    expect(second.project.sandboxes).toContain(renamed)
  }),
)
```

</details>

The existing `project.test.ts` suite (36 tests) is green alongside it.

## On the test conflict

I don't think this collides with `project.test.ts:344` ("separate clones of the same repo should share project ID"). Genuine clones still resolve to the same ID under any fix here — the question is only which dire

Just hit the same thing on my machine — adding a second data point and a workaround in case it helps others stuck waiting on the upstream fix.

**My numbers (measured, not estimated):**
- 68,150 orphaned `.dylib` files in `$TMPDIR`, totaling ~240 GB
- Each ~4 MB, all created within ~5 days (2026-07-28 → 2026-08-02)
- Same naming pattern: `.5bffffffffff....-00000000.dylib`

Same artifact as @magoz. `codesign -dvv` on a sample:

```
Identifier=libopentui.dylib
TeamIdentifier=not set
```

(Ad-hoc signature — consistent with Bun's dlopen materialization, not a macOS system mechanism.)

**Root cause is upstream in Bun, not opentui directly:**
Each time Bun loads an embedded native lib via `dlopen` (bun:ffi), it materializes a new hidden temp copy named `<hash>-<counter>.dylib` and never cleans them up. `@opentui/core` loads `libopentui.dylib` this way, so every opencode2 session leaks more copies. Tracked in:
- oven-sh/bun#29585
- oven-sh/bun#30962
- oven-sh/bun#29587 (fix PR, not yet merged)

So upgrading opencode/bun won't help until that PR lands.

**Workaround — hourly launchd cleanup (macOS):**
Since the fix is upstream and not imminent, I'm running a conservative hourly cleanup. Only matches the opentui temp pattern, and `-mmin +10` skips anything an active process might still be using. Posting in case it's useful:

\`\`\`bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
# Only cleans Bun/opentui ad-hoc temp copies; leaves everything else untouched
find /private/var/folders/*/*/T/ \
  -maxdepth 1 \
  -name ".*-00000000.dylib" \
  -mmin +10 \
  -delete 2>/dev/null || true
\`\`\`

Verified: the pattern match is exact, `maxdepth 1` keeps it shallow, and `-mmin +10` preserves copies an active opencode process is using. Happy to help test once the Bun PR merges.

Thanks — there was a real bug here, though not in the composition state.

An IME can commit `한` as separate jamo (U+1112 U+1161 U+11AB) rather than U+D55C. `Intl.Segmenter` clusters those correctly but `Bun.stringWidth` was summing each codepoint, so NFD `한국어` measured 11 where the widget reports 6. Assigning that offset back doesn't clamp — it snaps the cursor to 0, which may be the glitch your users are seeing. Fixed in 28e4e83 by composing multi-codepoint clusters before measuring; ASCII is unaffected.

I don't think composition state is at risk: over a TTY the terminal renders preedit itself and only delivers committed text, so the textarea never sees a composition to break. This change touches measurement only — it doesn't intercept keys or change when text lands in the buffer.

## Concrete evidence from a real incident (2026-08-02, opencode v1.18.11 on Linux)

Same failure signature as this issue: our SQLite store grew to **5.45GB main DB + 5.48GB WAL (~11GB total)** because a runaway agent loop kept writing session state into the shared store and the WAL was never checkpointed.

Sequence:
1. An agent loop hit a transient `AI_APICallError: Internal Server Error` (provider error, deepseek-v4-flash via opencode-go) at 10:10:07 and entered a **silent infinite retry loop** (~94% CPU, 2 hours, zero log output).
2. The loop kept writing into the shared SQLite store (WAL mode). WAL never checkpointed because the writer never paused.
3. Every new opencode instance in the same project then opened the pathological DB and **aborted natively (SIGABRT, 'core dumped')** right after the boot line 'booting location services' — storage/session-list init, where the giant WAL gets read. No log line, no journal, no apport entry.

Intermittency matched DB state at launch (WAL size / stale writer locks).

Remediation (manual, destructive-safe): killed runaway PID, `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, `VACUUM` (reclaimed ~1.7GB freelist on a 5.45GB DB with 1,330,391 pages, page_size 4096), rotated logs. DB back to 3.6GB, integrity ok, WAL ~4KB.

## What would help
- **A size guardrail / auto-checkpoint** — WAL >100-200MB should trigger checkpoint or alert. Our post-incident watchdog now flags WAL >200MB as unhealthy.
- **auto_vacuum / periodic maintenance** (see also #36851, #31526).
- **Graceful handling of a pathological DB at startup** — native abort instead of an error+recovery path is what turned a storage problem into a hard crash (see #37821, #37822).

Happy to provide more data (DB schema stats, exact crash sequence) if useful.

## Confirmed on our side (opencode v1.18.11, Linux, 2026-08-02)

Same crash: opencode aborted natively (SIGABRT, 'core dumped') at startup, silently — no log line, no journal, no apport entry. Every dying instance stopped right after the boot line **'booting location services'** (session-list/storage init, where a pathological DB/WAL gets read).

Root cause chain on our machine:
1. Shared SQLite store (WAL mode) grew to 5.45GB main + 5.48GB WAL because a runaway agent loop wrote unbounded into it (silent retry loop, ~94% CPU, 2h).
2. New instances opened that DB → native abort at 'booting location services', intermittently, depending on DB state at launch.

This is storage-layer corruption/bloat, not app logic — which is exactly why it was silent: the native abort happens below the JS layer.

## What fixed it for us
- `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` + `VACUUM` (reclaimed ~1.7GB freelist, page_count 1,330,391 → compacted) + killed the runaway writer. DB 3.6GB, integrity ok, WAL 4KB, boot clean.

## Request
A startup recovery path would have prevented the crash entirely: on open of a pathological/oversized DB, checkpoint or rebuild-in-place instead of native abort. #37822 (auto-recover) covers the right direction — hope it ships soon. Happy to attach core data or reproduce on request.

## Same silent-retry failure mode observed (2026-08-02, v1.18.11)

Not the serve --service path, but the same disease: a session loop hit a transient provider error — `AI_APICallError: Internal Server Error` on deepseek-v4-flash via opencode-go at 10:10:07 — and retried **silently forever**: ~94% CPU for 2 hours, zero new log lines (last line 10:10:28.567, then nothing until killed at 12:35).

Collateral: the loop kept writing session state into the shared SQLite WAL store → **5.48GB WAL on a 5.45GB DB** (never checkpointed, writer never paused) → every other opencode instance in that project then crashed on boot (native abort at 'booting location services').

## The pattern worth fixing
1. **Silent retry**: no backoff, no max-attempts, no WARN/ERROR log, no stop-and-surface. Two hours of invisible CPU.
2. **Unbounded iterations**: the loop had 1,499 iterations across 8 sessions in ~3.5h before erroring, then retried forever.
3. **Shared-store collateral**: one looping session destabilizes every concurrent instance via the shared DB.

Our guardrails now: retry_on_errors includes 500 (bounded retries, then surface error), per-session iteration caps, and a WAL size watchdog (alert >200MB). Would love to see equivalent defaults upstream: capped retries with logging on provider errors, and a WAL/size guardrail in the store layer.
